cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Name What It Cost
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm not accepting 'sorry for the silence' as the whole answer. Tell me what those six weeks did to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My phone broke. Doesn't that explain it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll allow it as an explanation of your phone. Now explain what it was like to keep checking mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the part I needed. Now add that I kept rewriting my message to sound easier to answer. I need you to understand what I started believing about myself.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 rejects an event-only apology, A3 permits a phone explanation but demands the waiting-person account and A5 approves the first inference before requiring self-doubt acknowledged, using authority to adjudicate cost.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 device cause prompts A3 distinction between B phone and A experience; B4 fear of lost care produces A5 concrete repeated self-editing.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks whether the cause suffices and B4 responds with an emotional interpretation, allowing the conversation to develop rather than only resist.

heightening.evidence: B4 caring inference causes A5 the deeper consequence of trying to become more answerable, not a new unrelated complaint.

specificity.evidence: A1 six-week silence and A3 your phone/mine establish ownership clearly; A5 revised message is an actual described behavior.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 explanation of phone versus person gives some dry wit, but A5 is an earnest request with considerable wording.
